# Lab 6.3: Partition Management

## What We Are Going to Do
Set partition expiration and require a partition filter, then delete and copy single partitions.

## Steps

1. **[SQL] Require a partition filter and expire old partitions.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">ALTER TABLE lab06.trips_daily SET OPTIONS (
  require_partition_filter = TRUE,
  partition_expiration_days = 1095
);</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


2. **[SQL] Try a query without a filter.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">SELECT COUNT(*) FROM lab06.trips_daily;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   It fails: **"Cannot query over table … without a filter over column(s) 'trip_start_timestamp'"**. This protects against accidental full scans.

3. **[CLI] Delete one partition and copy another.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">bq rm -f -t 'lab06.trips_daily$20230101'
bq cp -f 'lab06.trips_daily$20230102' 'lab06.trips_hourly_copy'
bq query --use_legacy_sql=false \
'SELECT partition_id, total_rows FROM lab06.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.PARTITIONS
 WHERE table_name = "trips_daily" ORDER BY partition_id LIMIT 3'</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   Partition `20230101` is gone.

4. **[SQL] Delete a partition with DML.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL

<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">DELETE FROM lab06.trips_daily WHERE DATE(trip_start_timestamp) = '2023-01-03';</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   A DELETE that covers whole partitions is a cheap metadata operation.

5. **[Console] Edit the settings.** Open `trips_daily → Details → Edit details`. Change **Partition expiration** and untick **Require partition filter**.

## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Required filter | Unfiltered queries rejected |
| Expiration | Partitions older than 3 years auto-deleted |
| `table$YYYYMMDD` | Address one partition |
| Whole-partition DELETE | Fast and free |
